The two clocks sit left (start) and right (end) inside one pale-green rounded panel, with the number 1-4 in a small green circle at its top-left corner and the sentence with a blank below the clocks. RIGHT clock (end): minute hand on 9, hour hand in the same place, seconds hand on 6 (30 seconds). Only the seconds hand differs between the two clocks: 0 s to 30 s, so the blank is 30 seconds.

items.ncert_ref: Note for the Teachers - the seconds hand (p.157), worked example
items.question_text: Remo timed himself tying his shoe. (a) The seconds hand started on 3 and stopped on 8. How many seconds did he take? (b) On another try it started on 8 and stopped on 2. How many seconds?
items.reason: The example is about reading a seconds dial: both parts give only start and stop numerals in words, and part (b) goes past 12. A picture of the two dials with the start and stop hands changes how easily the child sees the 8-to-12 and 12-to-2 stretches. Its own diagram, although a teaching image of part (a) is kept (user decision 5).

diagram.manim_description: On a plain white (BG) 1920 x 1080 canvas draw two analogue seconds dials side by side, the left dial centred at (520, 470) and the right dial centred at (1400, 470), both drawn identically. Each dial: a circle of radius 330 px in INK, 7 px stroke, no fill. Minute ticks: 60 ticks, one every 6 degrees, each from radius 290 px to radius 314 px, INK, 2 px. Hour ticks: 12 ticks, one every 30 degrees, each from radius 271 px to radius 314 px, INK, 5 px. Numerals: 1 to 12 in INK, 50 px high, each centred on the circle of radius 231 px at its position (12 at the top, 3 at the right, 6 at the bottom, 9 at the left; numeral n is at n x 30 degrees clockwise from 12). Hub: a filled INK circle of radius 12 px at the centre. Draw no hour hand and no minute hand. Left dial: a dashed GUIDE (grey) start hand, 4 px, dashes 14 px long with gaps of 10 px, length 198 px, at 90 degrees (on 3); a red (#D62828) stop hand, 6 px, length 198 px, at 240 degrees (on 8); and a curved arrow in FOCUS, 5 px, along the circle of radius 92 px centred on the hub, running clockwise from the 90-degree direction to the 240-degree direction, with a filled arrowhead 22 px long at the 240-degree end. Right dial: a dashed GUIDE start hand (same style) at 240 degrees (on 8); a red stop hand (same style) at 60 degrees (on 2); and a FOCUS curved arrow (same style) along the circle of radius 92 px running clockwise from the 240-degree direction through 0 degrees (12) to the 60-degree direction, arrowhead at the 60-degree end. Under the left dial write (a) and under the right dial write (b), INK, 64 px high, each centred horizontally under its dial at y = 900. Write no seconds values and nothing else.
must_not_show: any seconds value such as 25 seconds, 30 seconds or 40 seconds
shaded sweep or any written working
an hour hand or a minute hand
accuracy_checks: every hand angle = numeral x 30: 3 -> 90, 8 -> 240, 2 -> 60
(a) the clockwise arrow from 90 to 240 spans 150 degrees = 25 seconds (LP: 40 - 15 = 25)
(b) the clockwise arrow from 240 to 60 passes 12 and spans 180 degrees = 30 seconds (LP: 20 + 10 = 30)
the two dials are identical except for their hands and arrows; the 12 numerals appear once per dial
diagram.alt_text: Two seconds dials: in (a) a grey start hand on 3 and a red stop hand on 8; in (b) a grey start hand on 8 and a red stop hand on 2, each with a clockwise arrow from start to stop.
diagram.render_note: Two parts share ONE image (a worked example has one diagram). Letters (a) and (b) are shown because the LP steps refer to the parts by letter. The picture gives only what the question gives (start and stop numerals); the grey dashed hand is the start, the red hand the stop; no seconds value is written. Same dial style as C45's picture, only larger there. The 12 numerals are listed once in visible_text but drawn on each dial.
